title: C: Arrays & Functions
description: How to hand a whole array to a function, and why the original array changes.
congratsText: Nice work. You can now pass an array into a function, say why the original changes, and explain why the size has to go with it.
objectives: Write a function that takes an array plus its size
Explain why a function can change the caller's array
Identify why an array's size must be passed in
Choose between a void function and one that returns a value
recap: An array function takes two parameters: the array and how many items it holds.
A function receives an array's address, not a copy, so edits reach the original.
Inside a function, sizeof measures an address, so the size must be passed in.
void functions change the array in place; a return type hands one value back.

sections.title: Passing an Array to a Function

chunks.text: A function that works on an array needs two things: the array itself, and how many items it holds. That is why the parameter list reads int arr[], int size.

check.question: Why does the function ask for a size as well as the array?
options: The array alone does not say how long it is
The size is only there to make the code readable

chunks.text: Inside the function the array has a different name. In main() it is scores. Inside the function it is arr. Same array, two names.

check.question: Does the function need a variable called scores to work?
options: No, it works through its own name arr
Yes, the two names have to match exactly

chunks.text: You call it with the array's name and the count. No brackets, no &: showScores(scores, 5);.

check.question: Which call hands the whole array to the function?
options: showScores(scores, 5);
showScores(scores[5], 5);

quiz.question: What does this program print?

chunks.text: Hand a function a plain int and it gets a copy. Changing that copy leaves the original alone.

check.question: After bumpValue(x) runs v = 999 inside, what is x back in main()?
options: Still whatever it was before
Now 999, the same as v

chunks.text: Hand a function an array and it gets the address of the first item instead. No copy of the items is made.

check.question: What does the function receive when you pass scores?
options: The address of the first item
A fresh copy of all five items

chunks.text: Holding the address means the function reaches the real array. So arr[0] = 55; changes the caller's array, with nothing returned.

check.question: bumpFirst() sets arr[0] = 55 and returns nothing. Does scores[0] change?
options: Yes, it is the same array
No, nothing was returned

quiz.question: Arrange the tokens to build a function that sets the first item of an array to 0.

sections.title: Why the Size Has to Travel With It

chunks.text: In main(), sizeof(scores) measures the whole block: 5 ints at 4 bytes each.

check.question: What does sizeof(scores) give you inside main()?
options: 20, the size of the whole block
5, the number of items in it

chunks.text: Inside the function, arr is only an address. So sizeof(arr) measures an address, not the array.

check.question: Inside the function, what is sizeof(arr) actually measuring?
options: How big a single address is
How many items the array holds

chunks.text: That is why the size has to be passed in. Leave the argument out and the compiler stops you with too few arguments.

check.question: You call showScores(scores); with no size. What happens?
options: It does not compile at all
It compiles and assumes 5

quiz.question: This runs inside main() on Dev-C++, where an int is 4 bytes. Type the number it prints.

chunks.text: The same arr[], size shape works for changing items, not just printing them: arr[i] = arr[i] + 5; inside a loop.

check.question: Does a function that changes every item need to return the array?
options: No, it edits the real one
Yes, or the edits are lost

chunks.text: A function that only reads the array works the same way, but sends one value back with return.

check.question: Which of these two needs a return value?
options: A function that totals the items
A function that adds 5 to each item

chunks.text: So the return type tells you the job. void changes the array in place. int hands one number back.

check.question: You see int total(int arr[], int size). What is this function for?
options: Working out one value from the array
Editing the items inside the array

quiz.question: addBonus() returns nothing. What does main() hold after the call?
options: marks is {75, 85, 95}, changed in place by the loop
marks is {70, 80, 90}, since the function got a copy
marks is {75, 80, 90}, since only arr[0] is reachable
marks is unusable, because nothing was returned to it
